papers.title: A module-based approach for post-omics, post-GWAS network-based gene classification.
papers.abstract: Complex traits and diseases are highly polygenic and understanding the full set of genes involved is a central challenge in biomedicine. However, due to sample size limitations and noise (technical and biological), experimental approaches for disease-gene discovery such as transcriptomics and GWAS result in long, noisy, heterogeneous gene lists, which may be trimmed to a subset of likely relevant genes while leaving several false negatives. Computational gene classification approaches, especially those using genome-scale molecular interaction networks, are promising avenues for complementing s
papers.summary: This paper presents a module-based computational approach that integrates post-omics and post-GWAS gene lists with molecular interaction networks to classify genes and reduce noise, thereby improving the identification of likely disease-relevant genes. The method leverages network modules to complement experimental gene discovery, addressing challenges like sample size limitations and false negatives.

papers.title: Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding.
papers.abstract: Genomic and protein foundation models (GFMs and PFMs) have demonstrated strong performance in learning the language of DNA and proteins, but their use in large-scale sequence generation is limited by the latency of autoregressive decoding. Because every token triggers a forward pass of a large Transformer, whose inference is relatively slow, long-sequence generation quickly becomes costly.
papers.summary: This paper introduces speculative decoding to accelerate inference in genomic and protein foundation models, reducing the latency of autoregressive sequence generation. By using a smaller draft model to propose tokens that are then verified by the large model, the method speeds up long-sequence generation without sacrificing accuracy.

papers.title: Innovative approaches to therapeutic target discovery amid the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a constant threat to global public health, requiring innovative strategies for therapeutic target identification. Hence, this narrative review discusses the application of structural modeling and artificial intelligence in the functional prediction of proteins encoded by multidrug-resistant bacterial genomes. Tools such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold have enabled high-accuracy three-dimensional structure prediction, facilitating the annotation of hypothetical proteins and the identification of conserved domains and catalytic sites. These computational approaches bridg
papers.summary: This narrative review discusses how structural modeling tools like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold, combined with artificial intelligence, can be used to predict the function of proteins from multidrug-resistant bacterial genomes, aiding in the discovery of new therapeutic targets to combat antimicrobial resistance. The authors highlight how these computational methods enable high-accuracy 3D structure prediction, annotation of hypothetical proteins, and identification of conserved domains and catalytic sites.

papers.title: Identification of novel HUWE1 variants in Turner-type X-linked intellectual disability.
papers.abstract: To characterize the clinical phenotypes and identify the genetic etiology in four unrelated families affected by Turner-type X-linked intellectual disability (XLID).
papers.summary: This study identifies novel variants in the HUWE1 gene as the genetic cause of Turner-type X-linked intellectual disability in four unrelated families, expanding the known mutational spectrum of this gene. The findings provide new insights into the clinical phenotypes associated with HUWE1 mutations and may improve genetic diagnosis for affected families.

papers.title: SynFlow: an interactive online genome structural variant viewer.
papers.abstract: Structural variations (SVs), including inversions, translocations, duplications, and large insertions or deletions, are key drivers of genome evolution and phenotypic diversity. With the increasing number of high-quality, chromosome-scale genome assemblies, the ability to detect and interpret SVs has become a crucial aspect of modern genomics. While SV detection has advanced, most visualization methods produce static plots that fall short when researchers, particularly in comparative genomics, need to interactively explore large datasets, zoom into specific genomic regions, or dynamically filt
papers.summary: SynFlow is a new interactive online tool for visualizing structural variants (SVs) in genome assemblies, addressing the limitations of static plots by allowing researchers to zoom, filter, and explore large SV datasets dynamically. It is designed to support comparative genomics studies by making SV interpretation more accessible and user-friendly.

papers.title: Evaluation of genomic characteristics of Escherichia coli associated with bovine mastitis and the potential utility of alternative antimicrobial methods.
papers.abstract: Mastitis is a disease that affects dairy cattle and can be caused by multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli, causing losses to the agricultural sector. To address this, research into new substances with antimicrobial activity is crucial. Thus, the objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of extracts of Commiphora leptophloeos, Amburana cearensis, Agave sisalana, and highly soluble polypyrrole (Hs-PPy) against E. coli isolates. Eight E. coli isolates from bovine mastitis and a standard strain were used. The presence of efflux pumps was investigated by ethidium bromide extrusion. Seque
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
papers.summary: This study evaluated the antimicrobial efficacy of plant extracts and a polypyrrole compound against multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from bovine mastitis, and investigated the role of efflux pumps in resistance. The findings suggest these alternative substances may have potential as therapeutic options, though further research is needed.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation Reveal that METTL9 Drives Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression via TGF-β/Smad-Mediated EMT Activation.
papers.abstract: Methyltransferase-like 9 (METTL9) has been implicated in tumor progression, yet its clinical significance, functional roles, and immunoregulatory functions in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear. This study aimed to integrate multi-omics datasets and experimental evidence to systematically evaluate the expression profile, prognostic value, molecular mechanisms, and tumor microenvironment (TME)-related functions of METTL9 in LUAD.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data and experimental validation to show that METTL9 is upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma and promotes tumor progression by activating TGF-β/Smad-mediated epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The findings highlight METTL9 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases.
papers.abstract: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is an epithelial ovarian cancer subtype that is frequently misclassified as extraovarian mucinous metastasis (EOM) because of overlapping features. To address this diagnostic challenge, we perform genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of 58 MOCs, 38 EOMs, and 18 mucinous borderline ovarian tumors (mBOTs) collected from six institutions. Methylation analysis defines two mBOT groups, one epigenetically similar to normal ovary and one resembling MOC. Unsupervised clustering reveals two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance in the in
papers.summary: This study uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling to distinguish mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) from extraovarian mucinous metastases (EOM), a common diagnostic challenge. The analysis identifies distinct methylation subtypes of MOC with potential prognostic relevance, and shows that mucinous borderline ovarian tumors fall into two epigenetic groups, one resembling normal ovary and one resembling MOC.

papers.title: Pansoma, a machine learning tool for identifying somatic variants using pangenome graphs.
papers.abstract: Somatic variant calling, the identification of mutations in non-germline cells acquired over an individual's lifetime, is critical for studying diseases, including cancer, and for developing precision oncology strategies. Traditional somatic variant calling methods rely on linear reference genomes, which do not adequately capture human genetic diversity and result in reference bias, compromising the accuracy of somatic variant detection. Recently developed graph-based human pangenome reference represents diverse genetic variants across human populations and has promised to drive advances in ma
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Pansoma is a new machine learning tool that identifies somatic variants using pangenome graphs, which better capture human genetic diversity than linear reference genomes. By reducing reference bias, it improves the accuracy of somatic variant detection, which is critical for cancer research and precision oncology.

papers.title: MeioBIOME: A snakemake workflow for the parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and host-associated bacteria/archaea.
papers.abstract: Microbes closely interact with every living organism, including meiofauna (i.e., microbial eukaryotes 38 μm - 1 mm in length), and influence the development, life cycle, and evolution of diverse metazoans. Together, meiofauna and their microbiomes, collectively referred to as the holobiont, underpin biogeochemical cycles and drive decomposition of organic matter. However, our understanding of the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of meiofauna microbiomes are limited, typically owed to low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys, which cannot accurately delineate bacterial taxa. Single-specimen holobion
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MeioBIOME is a new Snakemake workflow that enables parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and their associated bacteria/archaea from single-specimen holobiont samples. It addresses the limitations of low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys by providing a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-resolution genomic and metagenomic analysis, which will improve understanding of meiofauna-microbiome interactions and their ecological roles.

papers.title: EXCAVATE-HT: A Bioinformatic Pipeline to Identify Targetable Genomic Variants for Allele-Specific Editing.
papers.abstract: Allele-specific CRISPR/Cas editing is a powerful tool with great potential for treating genetic diseases and for uncovering the effects of allelic diversity. By targeting commonly inherited single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), a small number of gRNAs can treat many more individuals than targeting rare disease mutations. However, current tools for identifying common targetable variants and generating CRISPR guide RNAs (gRNA) have fundamental conceptual and technical limitations. Here, we introduce EXCAVATE-HT (EXtracting Common Allelic VAriants for Targeted Editing in High-Throughput) a bioi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EXCAVATE-HT is a new bioinformatic pipeline that identifies common, targetable single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for allele-specific CRISPR/Cas editing, overcoming limitations of existing tools. It enables a small set of guide RNAs to treat a larger patient population by targeting prevalent variants rather than rare disease mutations.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging role of spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, in understanding cancer epigenetics within the native tissue architecture. It highlights how these technologies can reveal spatially restricted epigenetic regulatory programs and their impact on tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions, addressing limitations of bulk and single-cell methods that disrupt tissue context.

papers.title: HPRC2: A human pangenome reference with near-complete coverage of common genetic variation.
papers.abstract: A pangenome reference overcomes the inherent limitation of any individual reference genome by integrating the variation present in a population. We present the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium's (HPRC) Release 2 (HPRC2), an openly available, second phase pangenome that is an approximately fivefold expansion in genome number over HPRC Release 1 (HPRC1) and measurable improvement in genome completeness, contiguity, and accuracy. Selecting samples with a principled algorithm prioritising common variant coverage, HPRC2 contributes 460 haplotypes that together capture over 99% of common variati
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The Human Pangenome Reference Consortium presents HPRC2, a second-phase human pangenome reference with 460 haplotypes—about five times more than the first release—that captures over 99% of common genetic variation. The resource shows measurable improvements in genome completeness, contiguity, and accuracy, and was built using a principled sample selection algorithm to maximize variant coverage.

papers.title: Identification of Potential Biomarkers for Rheumatoid Arthritis Based on Integrated Bioinformatics and Single-Cell RNA-Seq.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that causes progressive joint damage and systemic complications. Despite multiple treatment options, many patients fail to achieve sustained remission. Our study aimed to integrate bioinformatics and single-cell RNA-seq analyses to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets and explore bioactive compounds from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM).
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and explores traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) compounds that may modulate these targets. The findings offer new candidate genes and drug leads for improving RA diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Discovery of a DNA methylation episignature for Weiss-Kruszka syndrome.
papers.abstract: Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WSKA; OMIM 618619) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of ZNF462, a zinc-finger transcription factor involved in chromatin regulation and early embryonic development. WSKA is characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, craniofacial dysmorphic features (around 8) and variable congenital anomalies. Genome-wide DNAm profiling was performed on peripheral blood DNA from 9 WSKA cases with (likely) pathogenic ZNF462 variants and matched controls to look for differential methylation. Analysis using the EpiSign™ pipeline ide
papers.summary: This study identifies a distinct DNA methylation episignature for Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WSKA), a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by ZNF462 mutations. Using genome-wide methylation profiling on blood samples from affected individuals, the authors found a reproducible differential methylation pattern that can serve as a diagnostic biomarker. This adds WSKA to the growing list of disorders with epigenetic signatures, improving diagnostic accuracy and potentially offering insights into the condition's pathophysiology.

papers.title: RNA and Mitochondrial Reprogramming Associated with Azacytidine Treatment in Higher-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Aims: Treatment of higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (HR-MDS) with azacytidine (AZA) exerts significant effects on the epigenome, primarily through DNA demethylation and reactivation of epigenetically silenced genes. Beyond this established mechanism, molecular AZA-linked effects are increasingly being recognized. Materials and methods: Liquid chromatography combined with mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) was employed for the accurate assessment of various RNA and DNA modifications pre- and post-AZA treatment of an HR-MDS cohort (N = 8). Mapping of the AZA treatment-responsive regulatory pathwa
papers.summary: This pilot study used LC-MS/MS to measure RNA and DNA modifications in higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome patients before and after azacytidine treatment, revealing AZA-induced reprogramming of RNA modifications and mitochondrial pathways beyond its known DNA demethylation effects. The findings suggest additional molecular mechanisms of azacytidine action that could inform treatment response monitoring.

papers.title: Natural compounds as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers: From chemoresistance to precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Gynaecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial malignancies, remain major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality because of tumour heterogeneity, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. Epigenetic dysregulation, involving aberrant DNA methylation, altered histone modifications, dysregulated non-coding RNAs, and N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) RNA remodelling, contributes to these processes. Direct evidence that natural compounds modulate m⁶A machinery in gynaecological cancers remains absent and is considered a knowledge gap.
papers.summary: This review examines how natural compounds can modulate epigenetic mechanisms—such as DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs—in gynecological cancers, with a focus on overcoming chemoresistance and advancing precision oncology. It highlights a critical knowledge gap: direct evidence that natural compounds regulate m6A RNA modifications in these cancers is still lacking.

papers.title: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in Drosophila eugracilis.
papers.abstract: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in the D. eugracilis Apr. 2013 (BCM-HGSC/Deug_2.0) (DeugGB2) Genome Assembly (GenBank Accession: GCA_000236325.2) of Drosophila eugracilis. This ortholog was characterized as part of a developing dataset to study the evolution of the Insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway (IIS) across the genus Drosophila using the Genomics Education Partnership gene annotation protocol for Course-based Undergraduate Research Experiences.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a gene model for the raptor ortholog in Drosophila eugracilis, characterized as part of a dataset to study the evolution of the insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway across Drosophila species. The work was conducted using the Genomics Education Partnership gene annotation protocol in a course-based undergraduate research setting.

papers.title: Using Deep Learning Models of Gene Regulation to Guide Drug Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Background: Drug repurposing offers a cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic discovery, but most computational approaches do not model noncoding genetic variation. Because over 90% of genome-wide association study (GWAS) risk variants reside in noncoding regions, linking regulatory variation to therapeutic hypotheses remains a major challenge. Methods: We developed an integrative deep learning framework that links allele-specific enhancer prediction to candidate therapeutics through two complementary prioritization strategies, a transcription factor (TF)-based and a gene-based appro
papers.summary: This paper presents an integrative deep learning framework that uses allele-specific enhancer predictions from noncoding GWAS variants to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By linking regulatory variation to transcription factors and target genes, the approach offers a new way to connect genetic risk to therapeutic hypotheses.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of single cell-derived melanoma sublines reveals divergent and parallel genomic and epigenomic evolutionary trajectories.
papers.abstract: Tumor evolution is driven by various mutational processes, ranging from single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) to large structural variants (SVs) to dynamic shifts in DNA methylation. Current short-read sequencing methods struggle to accurately capture the full spectrum of these genomic and epigenomic alterations due to inherent technical limitations. To overcome that, here we introduce an approach to identify and analyze the genomic and epigenetic events in different stages of tumoral evolution from long-read sequencing of single-cell derived sublines. We then use it to profile 23 sublines of a mo
papers.summary: This study introduces a long-read sequencing approach to analyze genomic and epigenetic changes in single-cell-derived melanoma sublines, capturing structural variants and methylation shifts that short-read methods miss. It reveals both divergent and parallel evolutionary trajectories in tumor sublines, highlighting the complexity of tumor evolution.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for mouse embryonic stem cell pluripotency. It reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the transition between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: ROS-Centered Transcriptomic Regulatory Networks Linking Salinity Stress, Antioxidant Defense and Processability Traits in Salicornia spp.
papers.abstract: Salinity stress affects not only the survival and productivity of halophytic plants, but also the composition, structure and processability of their biomass. In Salicornia spp., salt-induced regulation of ion transport, osmotic adjustment, reactive oxygen species signaling, antioxidant defense, and cell wall remodeling can directly influence residual salinity, water retention, texture, extractability, drying behavior, and oxidative stability of plant biomass. However, most existing transcriptomic studies of Salicornia and related halophytes have focused mainly on salt tolerance mechanisms, whe
papers.summary: This study investigates how salinity stress shapes gene expression networks in Salicornia, linking reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and antioxidant defense to biomass processability traits. It reveals that salt-induced transcriptomic changes not only support survival but also influence residual salinity, water retention, and other properties relevant to industrial use of halophytic biomass.

papers.title: Circulating Tumor DNA as a Biomarker of Treatment Response and Minimal Residual Disease in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common subtype of aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma and is characterized by pronounced molecular heterogeneity that is not always fully captured by standard histopathological assessment. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is increasingly regarded as a promising liquid-biopsy biomarker that enables non-invasive molecular tumor profiling, assessment of tumor burden, dynamic monitoring of treatment response, and detection of measurable/minimal residual disease (MRD). Modern analytical platforms, ranging from PCR-based assays to next-generation sequencing
papers.summary: This review examines the use of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) as a liquid biopsy biomarker in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), highlighting its role in non-invasive tumor profiling, treatment response monitoring, and detection of minimal residual disease. It discusses various analytical platforms, from PCR to next-generation sequencing, and underscores ctDNA's potential to capture molecular heterogeneity beyond standard histopathology.

papers.title: MORF4L1, encoding a chromatin remodeler, is mutated in a recognizable dysmorphic neurodevelopmental disorder.
papers.abstract: Chromatin remodelers are increasingly recognized as key contributors to neurodevelopmental disorders, usually through de novo dominant variants. Mortality Factor 4 Like 1 (MORF4L1) is recognized for its role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. We identified a consanguineous Middle Eastern family in which a neurodevelopmental disorder with a distinctive dysmorphic phenotype segregated with a homozygous variant in MORF4L1.  The autosomal recessive inheritance sets it apart from most other chromatin remodeling disorders. Consistent with its epigenetic role, we also observed
papers.summary: This study identifies a homozygous variant in MORF4L1, a chromatin remodeler, as the cause of a distinctive neurodevelopmental disorder with dysmorphic features in a consanguineous family. The autosomal recessive inheritance pattern is unusual for chromatin remodeling disorders, which are typically dominant. The findings expand the genetic spectrum of chromatin-related neurodevelopmental conditions.

papers.title: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in Drosophila erecta.
papers.abstract: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in the May 2011 (Agencourt Dere_CAF1/DereCAF1) Genome Assembly (GenBank Accession: GCA_000005135.1) of Drosophila erecta. This ortholog was characterized as part of a developing dataset to study the evolution of the Insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway (IIS) across the genus Drosophila using the Genomics Education Partnership gene annotation protocol for Course-based Undergraduate Research Experiences.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a gene model for the raptor ortholog in Drosophila erecta, annotated as part of a course-based undergraduate research project. The work contributes to a dataset for studying the evolution of the insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway across Drosophila species.

papers.title: amR: an R package suite to predict antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens.
papers.abstract: Identifying bacterial antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is critical for diagnostics and treatment, but resistance is a complex trait arising from myriad mechanisms spanning multiple molecular scales. Existing computational approaches often function as black boxes and rarely explore cross-species or multi-drug patterns. We developed amR, an integrated R package suite that provides a complete framework from bacterial genome data curation to interpretable AMR predictions, enabling identification of resistance mechanisms across species and drugs.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed amR, an integrated R package suite that provides a complete framework for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens, from genome data curation to interpretable predictions. This tool addresses limitations of existing black-box approaches by enabling identification of resistance mechanisms across species and drugs, supporting multi-drug pattern analysis.

papers.title: A Pan-Methylome Framework for Population-Scale Bacterial Epigenomics.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic modifications furnish a hidden regulatory layer that shapes cellular fate and evolutionary potential without rewriting the genetic code. In eukaryotes, methylome maps have profoundly transformed our understanding of development, disease, and lineage diversification. In bacteria, which represent the most abundant and ecologically versatile forms of life, the epigenome remains a largely uncharted dimension. To enable population-scale comparison of bacterial methylomes, we develop a principled strategy to prioritize methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded, broadly conserved
papers.summary: This paper presents a new computational framework for comparing bacterial methylomes at population scale, focusing on methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded and broadly conserved. It enables systematic, population-level epigenetic analysis in bacteria, an area that has lagged behind eukaryotic methylome studies.

papers.title: T-DNA Analyzer: A Long-Read Sequencing Pipeline for Characterizing T-DNA Insertion Sites in Transgenic Crops.
papers.abstract: Molecular characterization of the transferred DNA (T-DNA) insertion sites is required for the safety assessment of genetically modified (GM) crops, yet conventional PCR-based methods are labor-intensive and limited in their ability to resolve complex structural variations. We present T-DNA Analyzer, an integrated bioinformatics pipeline that transforms long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi or Oxford Nanopore) into a comprehensive insertion site report. The pipeline implements a host-derived read filter that subtracts host-homologous vector regions to eliminate false-positive chimeric read cal
papers.summary: T-DNA Analyzer is a new bioinformatics pipeline that uses long-read sequencing data to characterize T-DNA insertion sites in transgenic crops, overcoming limitations of traditional PCR-based methods. It filters host-homologous vector regions to reduce false positives and generates comprehensive insertion site reports, aiding in the safety assessment of genetically modified crops.

papers.title: Integrating epigenetic and metabolic indicators for non-invasive endometrial cancer triage: a machine learning approach.
papers.abstract: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is a primary symptom indicative of endometrial cancer (EC), yet its diagnosis still primarily relies on invasive biopsy. This study aimed to develop and validate a non-invasive, interpretable machine learning (ML) model integrating local epigenetic (exfoliated cell CDO1 methylation) and systemic metabolic indicators for EC triage.
papers.summary: This study developed a non-invasive machine learning model that combines epigenetic (CDO1 methylation in exfoliated cells) and metabolic indicators to triage endometrial cancer in patients with abnormal uterine bleeding, potentially reducing the need for invasive biopsies. The model is interpretable and validated, offering a promising tool for clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling: Technologies, computation, and applications in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Cancer is an intrinsically heterogeneous disease characterized by distinct malignant subclones defined by specific genetic and epigenetic alterations, such as aberrant DNA methylation. Traditional bulk sequencing methods analyze large populations of cells in aggregate, yielding an averaged methylome signal that masks the rare but clinically significant epigenetic patterns driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. The emergence of single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing has driven a paradigm shift in oncology by providing the resolution required to dissect this
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell DNA methylation sequencing technologies, along with computational methods, are enabling the dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity in cancer, which is masked by bulk sequencing. It highlights the potential of these approaches for precision oncology, including understanding tumor evolution and therapeutic resistance.

papers.title: A generator-matrix causal-inference framework separates measurable aging biomarkers from mortality-driving latent dynamics in humans.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in computational geroscience is to distinguish molecular quantities that predict mortality from those that causally drive it. Epigenetic clocks and aging biomarkers are increasingly used as if they were that mechanism, yet this is rarely tested directly. This distinction also bears on competing theories of aging: damage/reliability (A), hyperfunction/mTOR-IIS (B-1), and information loss (B-2). Although individual aging proteins have been tested piecemeal, no study has asked, in one framework, what fraction of mortality is measurable, whether it is causal, and whether it is
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a generator-matrix causal-inference framework to separate aging biomarkers that merely predict mortality from latent dynamics that causally drive it, applied to human data. The framework tests competing theories of aging and quantifies the causal fraction of mortality, offering a new way to evaluate epigenetic clocks and other biomarkers.

papers.title: TNEAtlas: A Pan-cancer Database to Identify and Characterize Transcribed Non-coding Elements.
papers.abstract: Advances in precision oncology have underscored the need to move beyond regulatory frameworks centered on protein-coding regions and better understand regulatory mechanisms within the non-coding genome. To systematically characterize transcribed non-coding elements (TNEs) in cancer, we developed an automated computational framework that integrates 130 RNA-seq datasets from 26 cancer types and 16 human tissues and identifies more than 2 million intergenic TNEs. In parallel, we established the first pan-cancer TNE database, TNEAtlas, which annotates TNEs with epigenetic signatures and functional
papers.summary: TNEAtlas is a new pan-cancer database that identifies and characterizes over 2 million transcribed non-coding elements (TNEs) by integrating 130 RNA-seq datasets from 26 cancer types and 16 tissues. The database annotates these TNEs with epigenetic signatures and functional information, providing a valuable resource for studying regulatory mechanisms in the non-coding genome.

papers.title: Comprehensive epigenetic landscape of Sulfur Mustard (SM) exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes.
papers.abstract: Sulfur Mustard (SM) is a potent vesicant chemical agent with profound and complex toxic effects. Traditionally, its toxic mechanism has been attributed to DNA alkylation-induced cytotoxicity and genomic instability. However, growing evidence indicates that dysregulation of epigenetic regulatory mechanisms constitutes a central link in SM toxicity, particularly in its long-term and delayed effects. Our study establishes an in vitro SM exposure model and employs integrated multi-omics profiling-including six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and non-coding RNA analyses-to s
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive multi-omics characterization of the epigenetic changes induced by sulfur mustard exposure in human keratinocytes, revealing coordinated alterations in histone modifications, DNA methylation, and non-coding RNAs. The findings suggest that epigenetic dysregulation is a central mechanism in sulfur mustard toxicity, offering new insights into its long-term and delayed effects.

papers.title: Deciphering chromatin architecture and dynamics in Plasmodium falciparum using the nucDetective pipeline.
papers.abstract: High-resolution analysis of cellular chromatin structure is crucial for uncovering developmental and cell-type-specific regulatory networks. We developed the nucDetective pipeline to provide a comprehensive evaluation of chromatin organisation. This involves assessing nucleosome positioning, occupancy, fuzziness, and array regularity. The pipeline was benchmarked by analysing the chromatin structure of the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) during its erythrocytic development cycle. Pf is characterised by a unique chromatin landscape, exhibiting unstable nucleosomes and a geno
papers.summary: The authors developed nucDetective, a computational pipeline for high-resolution analysis of chromatin structure, including nucleosome positioning, occupancy, fuzziness, and array regularity. They benchmarked it on the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum, revealing its unique unstable nucleosome landscape during the erythrocytic cycle. This tool provides a comprehensive approach to studying chromatin architecture in organisms with atypical nucleosome organization.

papers.title: Automatic generation of model sequences for complex regions in assembly graphs with TTT.
papers.abstract: Recent developments have enabled the automated assembly of vertebrate chromosomes from telomere to telomere. However, for long, highly similar repeats, genome assemblers may leave tangles in the assembly graph and gaps in the assembly. In recently published genomes, such gaps are closed by manual graph curation, a process that is labor intensive, error prone, and sometimes infeasible. Consequently, important genomic regions may be misassembled or omitted. Here, we present the trivial tangle traverser (TTT) algorithm that finds optimized resolutions of assembly graph tangles. TTT uses depth of
papers.summary: The paper introduces TTT, an algorithm that automatically resolves complex tangles in assembly graphs, which are common in long, highly similar repeat regions of vertebrate genomes. This reduces the need for manual curation, potentially improving the completeness and accuracy of telomere-to-telomere genome assemblies.

papers.title: Draft genome sequence of the almond red leaf blotch pathogen Polystigma amygdalinum assembled from infected almond leaves collected in California, USA.
papers.abstract: We report a draft genome assembly of Polystigma amygdalinum, the causal agent of almond red leaf blotch. DNA extracted from infected leaves was sequenced using PacBio HiFi, and host-derived reads were removed bioinformatically. The 238.7-Mb assembly (90.8% BUSCO completeness) is highly repetitive (82.3%) and unusually large for an ascomycete.
papers.summary: This study presents the first draft genome assembly of Polystigma amygdalinum, the fungus causing almond red leaf blotch, assembled from infected leaf tissue using PacBio HiFi sequencing. The genome is unusually large (238.7 Mb) and highly repetitive (82.3%) for an ascomycete, with 90.8% BUSCO completeness, providing a valuable resource for studying this pathogen's biology and evolution.

papers.title: DeepGeSeq: Deep learning library for Genomic Sequence modeling and analysis.
papers.abstract: Deep learning methods have demonstrated significant potential in genomics, enabling broad applications such as sequence activity prediction, regulatory rule identification, and variant effect quantification. However, their widespread adoption is often hindered by the steep computational learning curve required for model construction, training, and downstream biological interpretation. Here, we introduce DeepGeSeq, a user-friendly Deep-learning library tailored for Genomic Sequence modeling and analysis.
papers.summary: DeepGeSeq is a new user-friendly deep learning library designed to lower the barrier for applying deep learning to genomic sequence analysis, covering tasks like sequence activity prediction and variant effect quantification. It aims to simplify model construction, training, and biological interpretation for researchers without extensive computational expertise.

papers.title: AniAnn's: alignment-free annotation of tandem repeat arrays using fast average nucleotide identity estimates.
papers.abstract: Satellite DNA has long posed challenges for genome assembly and analysis due to its low sequence complexity and poor mappability. These large heterochromatic arrays of tandem repeats are ubiquitous across eukaryotic genomes, yet remain understudied. Current methods for annotating satellite regions, and other classes of tandem repeat arrays, are limited in their ability to annotate divergent or novel sequences.
papers.summary: AniAnn's is a new computational tool that uses fast average nucleotide identity estimates to annotate tandem repeat arrays, such as satellite DNA, without requiring sequence alignment. It addresses the challenge of annotating divergent or novel repeat sequences, which current methods struggle with, potentially improving studies of these understudied genomic regions.

papers.title: Methylation clocks fail to generalize across genetically admixed individuals.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic aging clocks based on DNA methylation patterns across the genome have emerged as a potential biomarker for risk of age-related diseases, like Alzheimer's disease (AD), and environmental and social stressors. However, methylation clocks have not been comprehensively validated in genetically diverse individuals. Here, we evaluate a set of first-, second-, and third-generation methylation clocks in 621 AD patients and matched controls from African American, Hispanic, and White cohorts. The clocks are less accurate at predicting age in genetically admixed cohorts compared to the White c
papers.summary: This study evaluates the accuracy of DNA methylation-based epigenetic aging clocks across genetically diverse populations, finding that these clocks are less accurate in genetically admixed individuals (African American and Hispanic) compared to White cohorts. The results highlight a critical limitation in the generalizability of methylation clocks, which is important for their use as biomarkers in diverse populations.

papers.title: Assessing the influence of different alignment tools on the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm) has long been a commonly investigated biomarker in biomedical research. The current gold standard for DNAm detection is bisulfite sequencing which requires dedicated alignment tools that can handle reduced sequence complexity. One commonly used application of DNAm are epigenetic clock measurements. These clocks have been adapted by many fields for their specific needs, including forensic genetics. Here, epigenetic clocks were designed to help estimate the chronological age of a biological stain donor for investigative purposes.
papers.summary: This study evaluates how different alignment tools affect the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock, which estimates a person's age from DNA methylation in biological stains. The authors compare multiple bisulfite sequencing aligners and find that tool choice significantly impacts clock accuracy, highlighting the need for standardized alignment protocols in forensic applications.

papers.title: map3C: a computational tool for processing multiomic single-cell Hi-C data.
papers.abstract: The emergence of multiomic single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) methods, which simultaneously profile chromatin conformation and other modalities such as gene expression or DNA methylation, creates tremendous opportunities for studying the genome's structure-function relationships. Existing tools for processing multiomic scHi-C datasets lack certain key functions for downstream bioinformatics analysis. We present map3C, a software tool that incorporates additional key functions. Specifically, we demonstrate that map3C facilitates multiomic scHi-C processing, quality control, and identification of structu
papers.summary: map3C is a new computational tool that fills key gaps in processing multiomic single-cell Hi-C data, which simultaneously profiles chromatin structure and other modalities like gene expression or DNA methylation. It provides essential functions for quality control and identification of structural features, enabling more comprehensive analysis of genome structure-function relationships.

papers.title: The Clinical Phenotype and Genetic Analysis of Monogenic Non Syndromic Obesity Caused by MC4R Gene Variation.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to investigate the clinical features and genetic variation of a patient with monogenic nonsyndromic obesity caused by melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene variation. Additionally, this study aims to provide a reference for the diagnosis of the disease.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the clinical phenotype and genetic basis of monogenic non-syndromic obesity caused by a variation in the MC4R gene, providing a detailed case analysis. The findings offer a reference for diagnosing this specific form of obesity.

papers.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation profiling is a central tool for molecular classification of pediatric medulloblastoma. However, most reference datasets are derived from high-income countries, and the performance of established epigenetic markers in underrepresented populations remains insufficiently explored.
papers.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
papers.summary: This exploratory study performs genome-wide DNA methylation analysis on pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort, assessing whether established epigenetic markers and molecular classification schemes perform adequately in this underrepresented population. The findings highlight potential differences or confirmations in methylation patterns, emphasizing the need for more diverse reference datasets in cancer epigenomics.

papers.title: Targeting NOP14 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment and enhances the antitumor efficacy of PD-1 blockade in DLBCL.
papers.abstract: Nucleolar Protein 14 (NOP14), a highly conserved factor in eukaryotes, is essential for pre-18S rRNA processing and small ribosomal subunit assembly. Emerging evidence underscores its pivotal regulatory role in the progression of various malignancies. Nevertheless, its functional involvement in Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), particularly its capacity to modulate the tumor immune microenvironment, remains to be fully elucidated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of NOP14 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and finds that targeting NOP14 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment, enhancing the antitumor efficacy of PD-1 blockade. The findings suggest NOP14 as a potential therapeutic target to improve immunotherapy outcomes in DLBCL.

papers.title: Unveiling the aging-immune axis in irritable bowel syndrome: a multi-omics and machine learning approach to biomarker discovery and validation.
papers.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with an elusive pathophysiology. Although immune dysregulation and mild mucosal inflammation are recognized as important factors in IBS, the specific contribution of immunosenescence remains unclear. Prior MR studies on IBS focused on single molecular traits; however, an integrated multi-omics framework for aging-immune genes has not been applied. Here, we integrate cis-eQTL/pQTL/mQTL with machine learning and in vivo validation to identify putatively causal biomarkers and unravel the aging-immune axis.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data (eQTL, pQTL, mQTL) with machine learning to identify aging-related immune biomarkers for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and validates findings in vivo. It reveals a potential aging-immune axis contributing to IBS pathophysiology and proposes candidate causal biomarkers.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics analysis identifies APOE as a candidate link between lipid dysregulation and macrophage activation in inborn errors of metabolism.
papers.abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) are a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by metabolic dysregulation and high mortality. Despite extensive genetic discoveries, the molecular mechanisms underlying severe disease progression remain incompletely understood. Increasing evidence suggests that host metabolic states, particularly lipid dysregulation, can profoundly influence immune cell function and may contribute to impaired responses against intracellular pathogens.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative bioinformatics analysis to identify APOE as a potential molecular link between lipid dysregulation and macrophage activation in inborn errors of metabolism (IEM). The findings suggest that altered lipid metabolism may influence immune responses, providing a new avenue for understanding disease progression in IEM.

papers.title: Integrating genomic structural equation modeling and experimental validation to unravel the genetic basis of male genital lichen sclerosus.
papers.abstract: To investigate the genetic architecture of male genital lichen sclerosus (MGLSc) and to identify potential susceptibility loci, candidate genes, and biological pathways associated with disease pathogenesis by integrating genomic structural equation modeling (Genomic-SEM) with multi-omics analyses and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic structural equation modeling with multi-omics data and experimental validation to uncover the genetic architecture of male genital lichen sclerosus (MGLSc), identifying potential susceptibility loci, candidate genes, and biological pathways. The findings provide new insights into the pathogenesis of MGLSc and highlight promising targets for future therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Clinically interpretable deep learning for breast cancer missense variant pathogenicity prediction.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in breast cancer remain diagnostically challenging due to their functional diversity and complex genomic contexts. Conventional laboratory assays for evaluating pathogenicity are labor-intensive, costly, and often impractical for large-scale screening, creating a pressing need for accurate, scalable, and clinically interpretable computational approaches.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense variants in breast cancer, designed to be clinically interpretable. The model offers a scalable alternative to labor-intensive laboratory assays, addressing the need for accurate computational tools in diagnostic settings.

papers.title: Novel variants of TP63 identified in Chinese families with split-hand/foot malformation.
papers.abstract: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a group of congenital birth defects affecting the hands and feet, significantly impairing patients quality of life. The TP63 gene encodes the p63 protein, heterozygous TP63 variants can cause SHFM. The aim of this study was to identify TP63 gene variants in three Chinese families with SHFM.
papers.summary: This study identified novel TP63 gene variants in three Chinese families with split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), expanding the known mutation spectrum of this congenital limb disorder. The findings provide new genetic evidence for diagnosis and genetic counseling in affected families.

papers.title: Epigenomics-Guided Multi-Omics Integration Uncovers a Lipid-Metabolic Signature with Translational Utility in Bladder Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Bladder cancer (BLCA) exhibits marked heterogeneity, and current classifiers provide limited guidance for prognosis or treatment. Because epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring jointly shape BLCA biology, we sought to identify epigenomically informed biomarkers with functional relevance. Methods: Epigenome (genome-wide promoter DNA methylation) and matched transcriptome (RNA sequencing) profiles from tumor and adjacent normal samples were integrated to identify genes with concordant differential methylation and expression patterns. A survival-oriented machine learning fram
papers.summary: This study integrates genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic data from bladder cancer tumors to identify genes with concordant epigenetic and expression changes, then uses machine learning to build a lipid-metabolic gene signature with prognostic and potentially therapeutic utility. The work highlights how combining epigenomic and transcriptomic layers can uncover clinically relevant biomarkers in a heterogeneous cancer.

papers.title: Dorsal Root Ganglion as a Hub for Peripheral Sensitization: A Hierarchical Regulation Model and Translational Progress.
papers.abstract: The high attrition rate of analgesic candidates in clinical trials stems largely from a reductionist reliance on rodent models and a neglect of the spatiotemporal complexity of nociception. Positioning the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) as the core computational hub for peripheral sensitization, this review proposes a "Hierarchical Regulation Model" to integrate fragmented mechanisms into a systemic framework. We stratify peripheral sensitization into three interlocking tiers: an acute tier driven by ion channel functional remodeling (eg, Nav1.7/1.8, Transient Receptor Potential (TRP) family); an
papers.summary: This review proposes a 'Hierarchical Regulation Model' that positions the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) as a central hub for peripheral sensitization, integrating ion channel remodeling, transcriptional changes, and other mechanisms into a three-tier framework. It aims to address the high attrition rate of analgesic candidates by providing a more systemic understanding of nociception beyond traditional rodent models.
